Looking at this problem, I need to compute the conditional Shannon entropy $H[R_{513}, C_{513} \mid R_1, R_2, \ldots, R_{512}]$ for 1024 non-attacking rooks on a 1024×1024 board.

## Proof

**Setup and probability model.** Placing 1024 non-attacking rooks on a 1024×1024 board means every row and every column contains exactly one rook. The placement is determined by assigning each rook $i$ a row $R_i$ and column $C_i$, where $(R_1, \ldots, R_{1024})$ is a permutation of $\{1, \ldots, 1024\}$ and $(C_1, \ldots, C_{1024})$ is a permutation of $\{1, \ldots, 1024\}$. Under uniform random placement (equivalently, sequential uniform placement of each rook among remaining valid rows/columns), the row permutation and column permutation are **independent uniform random permutations**.

**Applying the chain rule.** By the chain rule for conditional entropy:

$$H[R_{513}, C_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}] = H[R_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}] + H[C_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}, R_{513}].$$

**First term: $H[R_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}]$.** The values $R_1, \ldots, R_{512}$ are 512 distinct elements of $\{1, \ldots, 1024\}$. Since $(R_1, \ldots, R_{1024})$ is a uniform random permutation, conditioning on the first 512 values leaves $R_{513}$ uniformly distributed over the remaining $1024 - 512 = 512$ values. Therefore:

$$H[R_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}] = \log_2(512) = 9 \text{ bits}.$$

**Second term: $H[C_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}, R_{513}]$.** The column permutation $(C_1, \ldots, C_{1024})$ is **independent** of the row permutation $(R_1, \ldots, R_{1024})$. Conditioning on any subset of row values (including $R_{513}$) provides no information about any column value. Thus:

$$H[C_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}, R_{513}] = H[C_{513}].$$

By symmetry of the uniform permutation, $C_{513}$ is uniformly distributed over all 1024 values, so:

$$H[C_{513}] = \log_2(1024) = 10 \text{ bits}.$$

**Combining.**

$$H[R_{513}, C_{513} \mid R_1, \ldots, R_{512}] = 9 + 10 = 19 \text{ bits}.$$

Equivalently, this equals $\log_2(512 \cdot 1024) = \log_2(2^{19}) = 19$.

$$\boxed{H[R_{513}, C_{513} \mid R_1, R_2, \ldots, R_{512}] = 19 \text{ bits}}$$
